notes.printed: Whole-answer accuracy is the share of samples with every step right; a chain is right only if every step line and the answer line are right. Both marking rules are shown side by side: the Deviation 2 rule, which is official, and the original rule, under which a step line written more than once fails even when the repeats are identical.

Intervals are 95% and unadjusted: cluster bootstrap over puzzles with
resamples, except Opus-medium and Sonnet-medium per-shape whole-answer intervals, which are Wilson (the file's interval field).

"(exact, post hoc; … puzzles)" marks a bootstrap interval that collapsed to one value (every puzzle right, or every one wrong), replaced by the exact two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson interval from free analysis 4 (post hoc; it changes no test). The count in the mark is the number of puzzles, not of samples (the conservative unit).
In Opus-medium's per-step chain cells the count in the mark is only the puzzles whose chain sample could be placed: the set's puzzles less the unplaceable chain samples (Panel 3).
"(zero width)" marks Opus-medium's q interval (Panel 4) and q^N bands (Panel 5), which collapsed to one value; free analysis 4 gives them no exact interval (post hoc):

q is each model's share of pieces right, estimated from the pieces puzzles only and pooled over the lengths; q^N is the independent-pieces reference and observed / q^N compares the observed whole-answer accuracy with it. The 24-step row is an extrapolation only; its label, quoted as stamped, says "dotted", and the figures draw the line dashed.

Pilot 1 markers are at 24 steps, exploratory, and ran before Lock 2 with a different rule mix, different sets and different timing; they never enter q. A preset is one setting of the puzzle generator (its rule kinds and dials). One marker pools Pilot 1's sets of three rule-set presets; the other only those of the one preset used later, whose rules the length sweep keeps at every length.
The sweep is descriptive (pre-registered as such); no test is run on it.
